The scalar C_mu(n): standard deviation of the imputed mean in units of sigma

Source: R/sdf.R
c_mu.Rd

\(C_\mu(n) = \sqrt{w_\mu' B w_\mu}\) so that \(\mathrm{SD}(\hat\mu) = C_\mu(n)\,\sigma\) (the true standard deviation of the estimator, a function of the unknown population \(\sigma\)). The plug-in standard error is \(\mathrm{SE}(\hat\mu) = C_\mu(n)\,\hat\sigma\); its reference distribution is the subject of a separate study. Exact (numerical integration); for the closed-form shortcut formula see c_mu_shortcut.

Usage

c_mu(
  n,
  scenario = c("S3", "S1", "S2", "S4", "S5"),
  method = "blue",
  moments = NULL,
  type = 7
)

Arguments

n

Integer sample size: at least 3 under S1 and S2, 5 under S3 and S4, and 7 under S5, under the default quantile definition. Any such n is computed exactly; see Details. Another definition may need a larger \(n\): where two reported values are the same order statistic (type 3 at \(n = 5\) under S3, for example) the BLUE is not defined and is refused.

scenario

Character. One of "S1" (min, median, max), "S2" (three quartiles), "S3" (all five). McGrath 2023 labels; note Wan 2014's C2/C3 are S3/S2 respectively. Also "S4" (the quartiles with the 10th and 90th percentiles) and "S5" (all five with the two percentiles), the names of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026) for Scenarios 5 and 7 of Balakrishnan et al. (2022); only the BLUE ("blue") is defined for these two.

method

Mean estimator preset; see estimator_weights. The default "blue" is the BLUE, the default estimator version of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026); "luo" gives the factor of Luo's shortcut mean estimator.

moments

Optional precomputed result of osmoments::os_moments(n, ranks) for the standard normal, at this n and at the ranks that the reported values use (at n = 4Q+1 under type 7 these are scenario_ranks(n, scenario)), or a list with its components alpha and B alone. The sample size, the distribution, the ranks, the location and scale and the shape of alpha and B are checked where the object carries them; a bare list is checked for its size only. The package keeps the moments it computes itself for the session, so repeated calls at one sample size integrate once without this argument.

type

The definition of the sample quantiles, an integer from 1 to 9 as in quantile; 7, R's default, unless a study states another.

Value

Numeric scalar \(C(n)\).

References

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

Examples

c_mu(25, "S2")                 # exact C(n) for the BLUE of the mean under S2
#> [1] 0.2150631
c_mu(25, "S2", "luo")          # the same for Luo's estimator
#> [1] 0.2150631
c_mu(25, "S2") * sqrt(25)      # inflation factor over sigma/sqrt(n)
#> [1] 1.075315
